question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & -6 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -5 & -2 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{34}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{34}=3$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 4 & -6 \\ 8 & -3 & 5 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -5 & -2 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -9 & 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 & 0 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 & 0 \\ -2 & 4 & -1 & 3 \\ -9 & 6 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{3+4}|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3|\begin{aligned}-5 & 5 & 2 \\ 10 & -7 & 6 \\ -9 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
